title: OpenAI Jalapeno details at Hot Chips 2026
gist: OpenAI detailed its in-house inference ASIC 'Jalapeño,' co-built with Broadcom, at Hot Chips 2026, revealing a roughly nine-month RTL-to-tapeout timeline, an architecture built around HBM4 and a spatial programming model, and performance positioning against Nvidia's GB200 and GB300 accelerators.

themes.theme: OpenAI's custom silicon push with Broadcom

insights.claim: OpenAI presented its in-house inference ASIC, Jalapeño, at Hot Chips 2026, built with Broadcom and designed specifically to be the best compute platform for OpenAI's own inference workloads rather than a general-purpose accelerator.
insights.speaker: S
insights.so_what: Confirms OpenAI is moving beyond being purely an Nvidia GPU customer toward vertically integrated custom silicon for inference, a strategic shift that could reduce OpenAI's long-term dependence on Nvidia and validates Broadcom's custom-ASIC business model with a top-tier AI lab customer.
insights.quote: OpenAI took the Hot Chips 2026 stage on Day 2 to detail Jalapeño, an in-house inference ASIC and system built with Broadcom and designed to be the best compute platform for OpenAI's own inference workloads.

insights.claim: OpenAI engineers Richard Ho, Ravi Narayanaswami, and Chris Leary detailed a roughly nine-month path from initial RTL to tapeout for the Jalapeño chip.
insights.speaker: S
insights.so_what: A nine-month RTL-to-tapeout timeline is unusually fast for a full custom ASIC and is a notable data point for benchmarking custom AI silicon development speed, relevant to comparing against other hyperscaler in-house chip programs (Google TPU, Amazon Trainium, Meta MTIA).
insights.quote: Richard Ho, Ravi Narayanaswami, and Chris Leary walked through the chip's roughly nine-month path from initial RTL to tapeout.

insights.claim: Jalapeño's architecture is built around HBM4 memory and a spatial programming model, and OpenAI positioned its performance against Nvidia's GB200 and GB300 accelerators.
insights.speaker: S
insights.so_what: Direct competitive benchmarking against Nvidia's current flagship GB200/GB300 platforms signals OpenAI intends Jalapeño as a genuine alternative for its own inference capacity, not just a supplementary or experimental chip—material for assessing incremental risk to Nvidia's share of AI-lab compute spend.
insights.quote: its performance positioning against NVIDIA GB200 and GB300, and an architecture built around HBM4 and a spatial programming model.

insights.claim: A forum commenter noted that OpenAI presented relatively few details about Jalapeño's design at Hot Chips 2026, given the significance of the reported timeline.
insights.speaker: S
insights.so_what: Signals limited public technical disclosure so far—investors and analysts should treat Jalapeño's capabilities as still largely unverified pending fuller specifications or independent benchmarks.
insights.quote: OpenAI presented few details about Jalapeno. What do You think about that timeline?
